finding.title: Assert digit interpolation in he.todaysLearning(5) test — it only checks isNotEmpty while the EN counterpart checks contains('3')
finding.why: The EN test explicitly verifies the {count} placeholder is substituted into the rendered string; the HE test for the identical method only checks isNotEmpty. If a translator or a bad ARB edit drops the {count} placeholder from lib/l10n/app_he.arb's todaysLearning message (leaving a static 'לימוד היום' with no digit), the HE test still passes while the equivalent EN regression would fail. In a bilingual app where Hebrew is the RTL-primary locale, the weaker locale currently gets the weaker regression check.
finding.recommendation: Change line 81 to `expect(he.todaysLearning(5), contains('5'))` to match the rigor of the EN test at line 49.
acceptance_criteria: he.todaysLearning(5) test asserts contains('5') (or an equivalent digit-presence check), not just isNotEmpty
Test fails if lib/l10n/app_he.arb's todaysLearning message loses its {count} placeholder on regeneration

finding.title: Add direct unit/widget tests for content_grouping.dart's groupItemsByNextLevel and for HierarchyBrowser
finding.why: Repo-wide grep for groupItemsByNextLevel(, collapseAmudLeaf(, itemDisplayName(, levelValueAt(, and HierarchyBrowser( inside test/ finds zero direct references. content_grouping.dart's only test file, coarse_unit_leaf_refs_test.dart, covers 2 of its ~8 exported symbols and isn't even AG-5-named for this source (the mirrored name would be content_grouping_test.dart, which doesn't exist). HierarchyBrowser is exercised only transitively, three levels down, through unrelated parent-widget tests (bulk_mark_screen_test.dart, recent_activity_and_hierarchy_panel_l1_test.dart, r2_panel_leaf_crumb_ellipsis_test.dart) — never directly. This is the concrete reason the maxBrowseDepth dead-branch bug (separate finding) and content_tree.dart's parent() off-by-one (separate finding, in the sibling keepAlive-provider file which likewise has no direct unit test, only story-acceptance coverage) went unnoticed: the pure logic they live in has no focused unit test that would exercise the argument or the ordering that triggers them.
finding.recommendation: Add test/core/content/content_grouping_test.dart covering groupItemsByNextLevel (including the maxBrowseDepth branch), collapseAmudLeaf, itemDisplayName, and levelValueAt directly; add a HierarchyBrowser widget test independent of HierarchySelectionPanel.
acceptance_criteria: test/core/content/content_grouping_test.dart exists and unit-tests groupItemsByNextLevel directly, including a maxBrowseDepth case.
A widget test pumps HierarchyBrowser directly (drill-down, navigateBack, autoAdvanceSingleOption, empty state) without going through HierarchySelectionPanel.

finding.title: Rename core/utils/date_utils.dart's DateUtils class off the Flutter SDK's own DateUtils name
finding.rule: AG-4 (public top-level symbol names unique across lib/)
finding.why: package:flutter/material.dart exports its own `abstract final class DateUtils` (src/material/date.dart:247, re-exported at material.dart:65) with methods like isSameDay/getDaysInMonth used elsewhere in this repo (e.g. monthly_activity_sliver_calendar.dart calls Flutter's DateUtils.getDaysInMonth). This project's core/utils/date_utils.dart declares a second, unrelated `class DateUtils` with different semantics (isSameLocalDay is deliberately UTC→local-day aware per the P5 streak-boundary pattern; Flutter's isSameDay is a raw field compare). At least 14 lib/ files and 25+ test files import both material.dart and this file unqualified; exactly one file (goal_setup_screen.dart:1) already needed `hide DateUtils` to compile because it calls the project's DateUtils.extractLocalDate. Any of the other ~39 files is one `DateUtils.` autocomplete away from either a hard "ambiguous import" compile error or — if an agent "fixes" it by hiding the wrong side — silently swapping in Flutter's timezone-naive comparison where the streak-safe local-day comparison was intended, a domain the whole file exists to get right.
finding.recommendation: Rename the project's class (e.g. LocalDayUtils) or fold its 4 static methods into DateTimeFactory in the same file, so it no longer shadows the Flutter SDK name. Remove goal_setup_screen.dart's now-unnecessary `hide DateUtils` after the rename.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn "^class DateUtils" learning_tracker/lib/` returns no matches (class renamed).
goal_setup_screen.dart's `hide DateUtils` clause is removed and the file still compiles, confirming no remaining ambiguity.

finding.title: auth_repository_impl_test.dart exceeds the 400-line AG-3 cap (536 lines)
finding.why: coding-standards.md's own stated rationale for AG-3 applies directly: at 536 lines the file exceeds a typical per-file agent read budget and mixes ~15 unrelated method groups (sign-in, sign-up, Google auth, email-link, action codes, display-name, delete) in one file. Deleting the redundant auth_integration_test.dart (companion finding) doesn't fix this — it's a separate file — this one needs its own split.
finding.recommendation: Split along the existing group() boundaries, e.g. keep email/password + Google sign-in/sign-out in this file and move the email-link, action-code, and low-level-passthrough groups into a second file such as auth_repository_impl_actions_test.dart.
acceptance_criteria: File(s) covering AuthRepositoryImpl are each <=400 lines

finding.title: Stop pinning the dead, unlocalized ChartTimeRange.displayName getter with a coverage-chasing test
finding.why: chart_data_test.dart's own header says it exists to 'cover' previously-uncovered lines — its four tests simply assert the literal English strings the source hardcodes ('7 Days'/'30 Days'/'All Time'), the textbook tautological pattern (compare-against-what-the-source-literally-returns). Worse, the getter under test is dead: the only real caller, recent_activity_screen.dart, ignores ChartTimeRange.displayName entirely and switches through proper AppLocalizations getters (l10n.chartLast7Days etc.) instead. So this test spends 25 lines locking in a hardcoded-English getter that (a) no production code calls and (b) would violate AX-2 the moment anyone wired it up, and its passing status gives false confidence.
finding.recommendation: Delete chart_data_test.dart together with the ChartTimeRange.displayName getter itself, since recent_activity_screen.dart already has the correct localized replacement — don't keep a passing test whose only job is protecting a hardcoded-English string from ever being fixed.
acceptance_criteria: Either ChartTimeRange.displayName and its test are removed, or the getter is rebuilt on AppLocalizations and the test asserts against l10n fixtures instead of literal English.
